title: A root names its languages in _root.md and the pack stops, stems and folds its questions by them, with a tiny German and Polish fixture root
goal: _root.md may carry languages: en, de (default en = today's behaviour, byte-identical packs for every existing root). Per-language data under _tools/lang/<code>/ for de and pl (stop words, suffix rules, optional folding variants such as ö/oe and ł/l), and a root may bring its own profile in the same format under its _retrieval/lang/<code>/. Stop words are the union of the served roots' languages; each indexed unit is stemmed by its own root's profile and the query once per root it is matched against; a folding variant counts as present like an alias and is never a key word. A root naming a code with no profile is refused, naming the code and the codes that exist. A tiny German and a tiny Polish fixture root, with their own held-out questions and eval outside the public held-out file, answer good where the fact is present and none where it is not; the public eval shares and the test ids stay unchanged.

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import kbcommon
miss = [d for d in ('de', 'pl') if not os.path.isdir('_tools/lang/' + d)]
miss and sys.exit('no profile data under _tools/lang/ for %s' % miss)
try:
    de, pub = kbcommon.load_root('_tools/fixtures/lang/de'), kbcommon.load_root('kb/public')
except kbcommon.RootError as e:
    sys.exit('root not loadable: %s' % e)
langs = lambda r: tuple(getattr(r, 'languages', ()) or ())
langs(de) == ('de',) or sys.exit('lang-de languages are %s, want (de,)' % (langs(de),))
langs(pub) == ('en',) or sys.exit('the public root languages are %s, want the default (en,)' % (langs(pub),))

import os, re, subprocess, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
DE, PL, OWN, BAD = ('_tools/fixtures/lang/' + n for n in ('de', 'pl', 'own', 'bad'))
def pack(roots, root, q):
    env = dict(os.environ, KB_ROOTS=os.pathsep.join(roots))
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/rag.py', 'pack', '--root', root, '--format', 'concise', q], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def head(o):
    return o.splitlines()[0] if o else '(no output)'

o = pack([OWN], 'lang-own', 'Ka lodu zu mapa?')
'coverage: good' in o or sys.exit('a root-owned profile (stop words ka, zu) did not give good: ' + head(o))

for code_, root in (('de', 'lang-de'), ('pl', 'lang-pl')):

gates.question: What happens when a root's languages names a code that has no data under _tools/lang/?
options: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist
Serve it with the English profile and print a warning
gates.recommendation: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist
gates.reason: because a silent fallback hides a typo as a quietly wrong verdict
gates.answer: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist

gates.question: Which language data ships in the repository, and may a root bring its own?
options: de and pl only, in _tools/lang/, the two the fixtures prove; a root cannot bring its own yet
de and pl in _tools/lang/ and a root may add its own under its _retrieval/ directory
A wider set (es, fr, it, nl) in _tools/lang/
gates.recommendation: de and pl only, in _tools/lang/, the two the fixtures prove; a root cannot bring its own yet
gates.reason: because untested stop lists and suffix rules cost correct verdicts and a root-owned profile can be added later without changing the format
gates.answer: de and pl in _tools/lang/ and a root may add its own under its _retrieval/ directory

gates.question: Do the German and Polish held-out questions count in the public held-out answer rate (lookup_heldout.csv, 86 of 99)?
options: No: the fixture roots carry their own held-out file and eval, the public rate and its sprint-review bar stay as they are
Yes: add them to the public held-out file
gates.recommendation: No: the fixture roots carry their own held-out file and eval, the public rate and its sprint-review bar stay as they are
gates.reason: because the public file measures English facts about Windows management and mixing in fixture questions would blur that bar
gates.answer: No: the fixture roots carry their own held-out file and eval, the public rate and its sprint-review bar stay as they are

notes:
Premise (plan time): key_terms('Wie lade ich X im Kartenskript?') -> ['wie','lade','ich','im','kartenskript'] (wie, ich, im count as key words) and key_terms('Kartenskripte laden Karten') strips no German suffix; the English question gives ['load','usermap']. Reproduces at the key-word level; the pack-level verdict needs this story's fixture. _meta() reads flat key: value lines, so languages needs a list parse. The unit cache key hashes STOP and the token patterns (kf_index.py _weigh_data): profile data enters that hash and INDEX_VERSION bumps. Readers of kbfacts.STOP keep the English base set if the union is a new function.
Operator 2026-10-27: g1 refuse an unknown code; g2 de and pl shipped plus a root's own profile under _retrieval/; g3 fixture roots keep their own held-out file. Order: after ST-yl6b2ues (kbcommon.py) and ST-q5o7z2mf (tools.md).
Checks 9 (rag.py eval) and 10 (perfcheck ids) pass before the work and pin behaviour that must stay unchanged; every other check fails before it with a one-line reason.
Contract the checks read: Root.languages is a tuple (('en',) default); fixtures _tools/fixtures/lang/{de,pl,own,bad} as roots lang-de, lang-pl, lang-own (code qq, stop words ka, zu; fact 'Lodu mapa `LoadMap`.'), bad (languages: xx). de facts: 'Ein Kartenskript laden Sie mit `LoadMap`.', 'Die Königin einer Karte heißt `MapQueen`.'; pl fact 'Skrypt mapy wczytuje się funkcją `LoadMap`.', stop word jak; each of de, pl has _retrieval/lookup_heldout.csv with 3 or more passing rows; nothing about deleting.
